questions.prompt: What does type stability mean in Julia, and how do you inspect it?

options.text: A function's return type (and local variable types) depend only on the *types* of its inputs, not their runtime *values*—inspected via `@code_warntype`

questions.prompt: Why are untyped non-`const` global variables a major performance killer in Julia?

options.text: Their type can change at any time, forcing every function reading them to use dynamic dispatch and boxing

questions.prompt: Which loop order is fastest for iterating a 2D `Matrix{Float64}` `A` in Julia?

options.text: Row-major (`for i in 1:m, j in 1:n; A[i,j]`)
Column-major (`for j in 1:n, i in 1:m; A[i,j]`—inner loop varies the first index `i`)

questions.prompt: Select all techniques that eliminate unnecessary heap allocations in hot Julia loops. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Preallocate output arrays and write in-place with `.=` (`out .= a .* x .+ b`)
Parameterize struct fields with concrete type parameters (`struct S{T} x::T end`) instead of abstract `Any`/`Real`
Use non-`const` untyped global accumulators inside inner loops
Use `@views` or `view(A, :, j)` instead of allocating slice copies `A[:, j]`

questions.prompt: In `BenchmarkTools.@btime sum(\$xs)`, why is `$` placed before `xs`?

options.text: To interpolate the local/global variable `xs` into the benchmark expression so global lookup overhead isn't measured

questions.prompt: What is type piracy in Julia, and why is it discouraged?

options.text: Defining a method for a foreign function (e.g., `Base.+`) on foreign types (e.g., `String, String`) that your package doesn't own—risking silent breakage across unrelated packages

questions.prompt: What is the Holy Trait pattern in Julia?

options.text: A zero-cost compile-time dispatch pattern using singleton trait types (like `IndexStyle(A)`) to dispatch on properties independent of the single-inheritance type tree

questions.prompt: What does `esc(expr)` do inside a Julia `macro`?

options.text: Prevents macro hygiene from renaming symbols in `expr` so it evaluates in the caller's scope

questions.prompt: When does a Julia `macro` execute compared to a normal `function`?

options.text: At parse/compile time, transforming AST (`Expr`) into new AST before type inference and LLVM codegen

questions.prompt: What is the key constraint on `@generated function` bodies in Julia?

options.text: The generator body only sees the *types* of arguments (not values), must be pure (no side effects/global state mutation), and returns a quoted `Expr`

questions.prompt: What does `Threads.@spawn expr` do compared to `Threads.@threads`?

options.text: Schedules an asynchronous `Task` on any available thread in Julia's work-stealing scheduler, returning a `Task` you can `fetch()`

questions.prompt: Why is `Threads.threadid()` unsafe as an array index (`buf[Threads.threadid()]`) in modern Julia?

options.text: Tasks can migrate between OS threads across yields/allocations (or exceed `nthreads()` with `:interactive` pool); use `Channel`, `ReentrantLock`, or task-local chunking instead

questions.prompt: Select all valid synchronization primitives for multi-threaded Julia. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Reading/writing a shared `Dict` concurrently from multiple threads without locking

questions.prompt: What does `ccall((:strlen, "libc"), Csize_t, (Cstring,), s)` do?

options.text: Calls a C shared-library function directly with zero wrapper overhead using Julia's native FFI

questions.prompt: What is `GC.@preserve obj begin ... end` used for when passing pointers (`pointer(arr)`) to `ccall`?

options.text: Guarantees the garbage collector will not move or collect `obj` while raw pointers to its memory are in use

questions.prompt: What does `@inbounds` inside a performance-critical loop do, and what is its precondition?

options.text: Elides array bounds checks for speed—ONLY safe when indices are mathematically proven in-bounds (violating it causes memory corruption/UB!)

questions.prompt: What does `@simd for i in eachindex(a, b)` permit the compiler to do?

options.text: Reassociate floating-point reductions and emit SIMD vector instructions when iterations are independent

questions.prompt: Why does Julia distinguish `isbits(T)` types (like `Float64`, `SVector{3, Float64}`, `Tuple{Int, Int}`)?

options.text: They contain no heap references, so arrays `Vector{T}` store them packed inline contiguously with zero per-element GC tracking

questions.prompt: What is 'world age' in Julia?

options.text: A monotonic counter tracking method table updates so compiled code sees a consistent method set and `eval`ed methods aren't called directly in the same world without `Base.invokelatest`

questions.prompt: What does `Base.@propagate_inbounds` on a helper function `getval(A, i)` do?

options.text: Allows a caller's `@inbounds` context to propagate into `getval` while still checking bounds when called normally

questions.prompt: What is a 'method invalidation' in Julia package loading?

options.text: When defining a new method (especially overly broad ones on `Any`) forces Julia to recompile previously compiled callers that depended on an earlier dispatch assumption

questions.prompt: What does `StaticArrays.SVector{3, Float64}` improve over `Vector{Float64}` of length 3 in physics/geometry?

options.text: Fixed size known in the type (`3`), so it lives in registers/stack with zero heap allocations and fully unrolled math

questions.prompt: Select all ways to reduce Time-To-First-Execution (TTFX) / startup latency in Julia applications. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Avoid type-unstable code and method invalidations in your package
Build a custom sysimage with `PackageCompiler.jl` for CLI/server deployments

questions.prompt: What does `FunctionWrappers.jl` or `::Function` field pitfall teach about storing callbacks in a `struct`?

options.text: In Julia, every function has its own singleton type (`typeof(sin) !== typeof(cos)`), so typing a field `f::Function` is abstract; parameterize `struct S{F} f::F end`!

questions.prompt: What does `Base.inferencebarrier(x)` or `Ref{Any}(x)[]` do?

options.text: Intentionally hides `x`'s concrete type from the compiler (useful when benchmarking or preventing excessive specialization)

questions.prompt: Why does `AbstractArray{T, N}` allow writing one algorithm that works on `Array`, `SubArray`, `CuArray` (GPU), and `SparseMatrixCSC`?

options.text: Generic code written against `AbstractArray` interfaces (`size`, `axes`, `eachindex`, broadcasting) specializes per concrete array type via multiple dispatch

questions.prompt: What does `Channel{T}(N)` provide for concurrent pipelines in Julia?

options.text: A thread-safe bounded (or unbuffered `0`) FIFO queue for passing `T` items between `Task`s

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `Compat.jl` in Julia open-source packages?

options.text: Providing forward-compatibility macros/shims so packages support multiple Julia LTS and current minor versions

questions.prompt: What does `JET.jl` (`@report_opt`, `@report_call`) check statically?

options.text: Type errors, undefined methods, and runtime-dispatch/type-instability hotspots without needing to execute every branch

questions.prompt: What does `@nospecialize(x)` on a rarely-called error/logging helper parameter prevent?

options.text: Generating redundant compiled specializations for dozens of concrete argument types, reducing compile time and memory

questions.prompt: Why can `push!(v, item)` in a loop be slightly slower than preallocating `v = Vector{T}(undef, n)` when `n` is known?

options.text: Preallocating `Vector{T}(undef, n)` (or `sizehint!(v, n)`) avoids geometric capacity doublings and reallocations

questions.prompt: What does `Vector{Float64}(undef, n)` do when creating a new array?

options.text: Allocates space for `n` `Float64`s without spending time zero-initializing them (you must write every slot before reading!)

questions.prompt: What does `Base.issingletontype(T)` / singleton types (structs with 0 fields like `struct CPU end`) cost at runtime?

options.text: Zero bytes (`sizeof(CPU()) == 0`); Julia passes them purely in the type system for zero-cost dispatch

questions.prompt: Select all best practices for writing fast, idiomatic Julia packages. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Store all state in untyped global variables
Keep functions small, type-stable, and pure where possible

questions.prompt: What does `Test.@inferred f(x)` verify in a test suite?

options.text: That the return type inferred by Julia's compiler matches the actual runtime return type of `f(x)`

questions.prompt: What does `mul!(C, A, B)` from `LinearAlgebra` do compared to `C = A * B`?

options.text: Performs matrix multiplication writing directly into preallocated `C` with zero output allocation

questions.prompt: What is `Base.Meta.@lower` or `Meta.parse` used for?

questions.prompt: Why does `Profile.@profile` sometimes show high time in `jl_apply_generic`?

options.text: Dynamic dispatch caused by a type instability (compiler couldn't statically resolve the callee method)
